title: Choose the visual world for Second Brain
question: The roll assigned the card catalogue: every source becomes an index card with a call number. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Fiches bristol · the card catalogue
options.lineage: Library card catalogues and the ruled bristol index cards French-school students revise with
options.thesis: Every source is a fiche with a call number; every answer is written on a working card with its cited fiches pulled from the drawer beside it.
materials: ruled bristol card stock with the red header line
blue-grey steel catalogue drawers with label holders
a rod hole at each card's foot
options.viewport: Left: a steel cabinet rail of module drawers grouped by teaching unit, with card counts and new-since-sync marks. Centre: the working card, question on its red header line, answer typed on its ruled lines. Right: the cited fiches, each with a call number like PROB2 · CH1 · p. 3.
options.risk: Can slide into costume if the card texture turns decorative; the ruling, colour-per-module and call numbers must each do a job or be cut.

raised.raise: Citation numbers sit in a strict margin column on the card's red margin line, aligned to the paragraph they support.
Tracing runs both ways: focus a fiche and every sentence that leans on it lights up in the answer.
The library drawer is a fixed-column grid (call number, title, parts, status) whose columns never move; only rows change.
Stillness while reading: the working card never moves while an answer streams; past cards recede by depth, not clutter.
You handle the object: a fiche flips to show the full passage on its back, the gesture future flashcards will reuse.
Changes stay lit until noticed: newly synced material keeps its mark in the drawer until you open it.

options.label: The lab notebook (Jupyter)
options.lineage: Jupyter notebooks, the data-science student's daily working surface
options.thesis: Each question is an input cell and each answer an executed output, its sources returned like a cell's printed results.
options.viewport: A notebook of cells scoped to one module kernel: run a question with Shift+Enter, the output streams below with numbered source outputs.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: it looks like work rather than revision, and code-editor grammar handles Arabic right-to-left prose poorly.

options.label: Orizuru fold sequence
options.thesis: One sheet passing through numbered folds from flat square to finished crane.
options.viewport: A strict numbered margin column beside a centred diagram.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a student revising probability does not recognise themself in paper folding, and answers are not step sequences.
options.risk: Pure metaphor; nothing in the product folds.
options.kept: Its strict numbered margin column, now carrying the citations.

options.label: Tensegrity column
options.thesis: Trace any load to its counterforce through a network of rods and cords.
options.viewport: Annotations pinned to nodes on leader lines.
options.case: Fuses partly: tracing a claim to its source maps well, but the sculpture means nothing to the student.
options.risk: Engineering-art costume over a study tool.
options.kept: Two-way tracing between claims and the sources they lean on.

options.label: Split-flap concourse
options.thesis: Rows ranked by time on a board whose columns never move.
options.viewport: A ruled board of rows cascading on change.
options.case: Fuses poorly: answers are prose, not departures; it only suits the library list.
options.risk: Novelty cascade on a reading surface.
options.kept: Fixed columns that never move in the library drawer.

options.label: Cracktro scroller queue
options.thesis: One still line of bitmap text over drifting depth layers.
options.viewport: Layers stacked by depth, the front plane still while read.
options.case: Fuses poorly: bitmap type cannot carry dense French, English and Arabic course text for hours.
options.kept: Stillness while reading, and depth as state for past answers.

options.label: Leather reading shelf
options.thesis: Digital things rendered as loved physical objects on a shelf.
options.viewport: Books on shelves, pages that curl.
options.case: Fuses poorly: lamplight and leather are the warm-bookish rut, and texture fights formula-heavy reading.
options.kept: Handling the object: flipping a fiche to read its back.

options.label: Boarding pass and gate board
options.thesis: A segmented pass plus a board that reranks in place and holds changes lit.
options.viewport: Citations as pass segments, the library as a live board.
options.case: Fuses partly: good for sync freshness, but a student does not recognise revision as travel.
options.risk: Airport chrome on a study desk.
options.kept: Newly synced material stays marked until you open it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A chat-with-your-notes assistant: centred conversation column, source chips under each answer, notebooks in a sidebar.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of modules, centred chat thread, input pinned at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI chat product by design.
